key_insight: VideoRAE shows that frozen Video Foundation Model representations can be repurposed into compact latent spaces for video generation, instead of relying on traditional 3D-VAE latents. This can preserve richer semantic and spatio-temporal structure while still supporting reconstruction and generative modeling.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the limitation of conventional 3D-VAEs, which are trained mainly for pixel reconstruction and often fail to capture high-level semantics and temporal structure needed for strong video generation.
method: Use pretrained Video Foundation Model features as the latent representation backbone for video generation.
Transform frozen VFM representations into a reconstruction-capable, compact latent space via a Representation Autoencoder (RAE) framework.
Replace or augment standard 3D-VAE latents to better retain semantic and spatio-temporal information for downstream generative modeling.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a path to more expressive video latents that can improve generation quality without training a video encoder from scratch. It is especially relevant for building video generative systems that need both compactness and stronger temporal semantics.

paper_title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders
paper_authors: Zhihao Xie, Junfeng Wu, Xinting Hu, Junchao Huang, Li Jiang
